Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS: The December 13, 2017 FOMC statement remains moderately positive on growth and labor markets with cautious language on below-target inflation and “gradual” hikes consistent with standard reaction functions. However, the October 2017 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to a more mixed credit backdrop that tempers the tone: banks eased standards for C&I loans amid competition (supportive for business credit), but tightened terms for credit card and auto loans and reported weaker demand for several loan purposes—including credit card and auto, as well as inventory, accounts receivable, plant/equipment investment, and M&A—citing the economic outlook, portfolio quality, and risk tolerance. This pattern suggests no broad credit crunch, yet softer consumer credit conditions and waning demand for investment-related financing could modestly weigh on household spending and future capex relative to the FOMC’s constructive baseline. Two dovish dissents reinforce this risk-aware stance. Netting these factors, the communication remains credible and constructive but is more balanced once SLOOS headwinds are considered.
